This happens quite frequently actually, the real problem is there's a huge legal difference between 2 different terms that can be both traslated to "seizure", those are "sequestro" and "confisca".

First one (sequestro) means those money are just frozen, so noone can use them until a trial is concluded, it's a very good thing per se but the problem is noone knows what happens to those money when the trial is over.

Second one (confisca) means those money are given back to the Government who uses them to refund losses (depending on the trial outcomes) and/or uses them for social purposes.

This specific article is about "sequestro" (money just frozen), the most frequent case. Secon one (confisca) is always desirable but happens very rarely unfortunately.

Edit: corrected a switching mistake on the 2 terms.
So, essentially the assets have been frozen? The parties can't access them but nor has the government conducted a seizure?

Yes to both questions.

We have to wait for the trial to see if this kind of seizure (sequestro) will turn into the second one (confisca).

Until we get an all-inclusive app like Mac users have in OpenEMU, it seems we're stuck mashing up multiple emulators separately or using Libreto/RetroArch to set things up on our own. PC users have been begging for a nice emulation setup with a competent GUI for years, but it seems that our dreams may soon become reality.

There is a nice frontend in the works for PC users called Snowflake. It is actively being worked on [you can contribute to the project via GitHub], and definitely a project to keep an eye on as there is an alpha version slated to be released sometime soon.

There is also a frontend project for those who use RetroArch called Phoenix. The link goes to their GitHub repository where you can follow or contribute to the progress, but it also hasn't been officially released yet.
